0.content:
Natlan Cuisine (also: Natlanese food, Natlanese cuisine, Natlan dishes, Natlan food): Natlanese food is hearty and filling, heavy on starch and meat. Grainfruit, a plant named for the giant grains along its cob, is the staple and the base of many dishes, including tatacos, grainfruit meat soup and the Hot Spring O'Clock pizza. Cacahuatl, bitter and complex, flavours sweets and drinks such as volcano cake, saurus crackers and xocoatl. The main restaurant is Zakan's Street Bites, a food stall run by the innkeeper Chanca.

Food in Natlan sits in everyday tribal life: warriors, pilgrims and travellers eat at the stadium inn, and individual tribes have their own snacks. Saurians also figure in the food culture, appearing as shapes on crackers and as a motif on pizza.

Most signature dishes are simple enough that, according to Chanca, almost everyone in Natlan knows how to make tatacos. Item texts treat food as comfort and good cheer, with sayings, shared meals and snacks that calm the nerves.

Detail on specific dishes, ingredients and shops is in the sections and entries below. Documented regional variation is thin and mostly limited to a few tribe-linked snacks.

Practice: Grainfruit is the base of tatacos, grainfruit meat soup and Hot Spring O'Clock. Tatacos are thin tacos baked first, filled with vegetables and grilled shrimp, then topped with a sauce. Grainfruit meat soup comes with a choice of broths and side dishes, but must contain lots of grainfruit. Cacahuatl goes into sweeter things: volcano cake, saurus crackers and the drink xocoatl.

Tatacos' item text says it is hard to say what is more common in Natlan, phlogiston or tatacos, and quotes a Natlanese saying that life might disappoint but tatacos never will. Xocoatl is made from cacahuatl ground and blended with spices; the name means "bitter water" and stayed after added sugar made it sweet, fragrant and popular. Saurus crackers are light, crispy, sweet crackers stamped with saurian patterns; the text wonders whether saurians really eat crackers. Volcano cake is a baked cake with a hard outer layer and a soft molten filling, served with something cold on top to play the "ash cloud".

Cacahuatl's seeds, once fermented and baked, are made into delicacies and are considered the most valuable part; its white flesh can also be pressed for juice. Quenepa berries (blue, juicy, growing in large numbers near the Scions of the Canopy and shaped like flamegranates) are also eaten, and flamegranates less so; the culture page says flamegranate fills whatever it goes into with phlogiston. Embercore flower nectar is extremely sweet and leaves a burning sensation on the lips and tongue, a flavour popular among the tribes. Hot Spring O'Clock is a grainfruit-and-cheese pizza with a little Koholasaurus picture drawn on it, meant to be eaten hot for the feeling of a soak in a hot spring.

Grainfruit meat soup, per its text, delivers soft meat, crunchy vegetables and a lively spiciness. Puff pops take the "pop" in their name from grainfruit kernels bursting under high heat; their unpredictable flavours are said to raise the heart rate, which is why they are popular. The xocoatl text also describes a rich cacahuatl scent and a silky, creamy sweetness. The Nahuatl word meaning "bitter water" behind the name is the wiki's observation, not an in-world statement.

Regional variation: The Scions of the Canopy are linked to puff pops, and the People of the Springs to the Hot Spring O'Clock pizza. Both are cooking recipes unlocked through reputation with those tribes. The culture page adds that the Collective of Plenty, with its plentiful crops, is fond of mushrooms because Varesa's family orchard came to grow berryshrooms after an unforeseen incident involving Bifrons.

Volcano cake's recipe is found in the Tezcatepetonco Range and saurus crackers' in the Toyac Springs area, so dishes are spread across regions, but their texts do not claim tribal ownership. No source read names signature dishes for the Children of Echoes, Flower-Feather Clan or Masters of the Night-Wind.

Scene use: Use warm, filling, smoky detail: a baked taco shell, spicy broth, a bitter-sweet cup of xocoatl, grainfruit kernels popping in the heat.

Natlanese hospitality tends toward generosity and comfort after hardship. Let visitors from other nations notice how hearty the food is, and keep flavours consistent with item texts (cacahuatl is bitter, then sweetened; grainfruit is the base). Do not invent ritual or tribal food taboos that canon does not state.

Warriors resting between battles and pilgrims are natural customers at the Weary Inn and its food stall. A scene set after the fighting can have old comrades eating together while carrying their injuries, as Chanca describes.

Examples: Chanca teaching the Traveler how to make tatacos rather than handing over a finished one. Friends sharing puff pops. A traveller sampling xocoatl and wincing at the first taste, then smiling at the sweetness. A group splitting a Hot Spring O'Clock pizza.

1.comment: Natlan Cuisine: Zakan's Street Bites and Chanca
1.content:
Zakan's Street Bites is the main restaurant for Natlan, a food stall at the entrance of the Weary Inn in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame area. It is run by Chanca, an Ancient Name bearer and once a top-ranked warrior in the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame. A leg injury in her last battles in the Night Warden Wars forced her to retire, and she later took over the inn. The stall sells meals, ingredients and recipes such as grainfruit meat soup and xocoatl.

Chanca calls tatacos her personal specialty and teaches the Traveler to make them. She says she stayed at the inn free as a contestant, and tells pilgrims that friends of contestants can eat and sleep there at no charge. She says that after the battles ended many old comrades stop by for meals, injured but seemingly happy, and that she can only treat them to food now. A permanent 10% shop discount for players at maximum reputation with two of the six tribes is a gameplay detail.

2.content:
Tatacos are thin baked tacos, filled with vegetables and grilled shrimp and drizzled with sauce. They are Chanca's specialty and are described as a familiar part of Natlan life.

Item text includes the Natlanese saying that tatacos never disappoint. Citlali has a special version of the dish in gameplay.

3.content:
Cacahuatl is a Natlan crop with a bitter, flavourful fleshy part and seeds that, fermented and baked, become delicacies. Xocoatl is the drink made from it, originally a bitter spiced water and now a sweet, creamy, widely loved beverage that kept its "bitter water" name.

Ifa has a special version of xocoatl in gameplay. Its recipe is sold by Chanca.

4.comment: Natlan Cuisine: Grainfruit and grainfruit dishes
4.content:
Grainfruit is found all over Natlan and is the basis of grainfruit meat soup, Hot Spring O'Clock and puff pops. Grainfruit meat soup is a spicy mix of meat and vegetables with many broth and side-dish choices.

Hot Spring O'Clock is the People of the Springs' pizza topped with grainfruit and cheese, and puff pops are a Scions of the Canopy snack.

5.content:
Volcano cake is a sweet with a soft molten centre and a cold topping.

Its recipe comes from an Exquisite Chest in the Tezcatepetonco Range. The cake's text emphasises satisfaction and comfort.

6.content:
Saurus crackers are buttery, crisp, sweet crackers made with cacahuatl and grainfruit and shaped like little saurians.

Their recipe comes from an Exquisite Chest in the Toyac Springs area; the wiki also lists a dialogue option with Sorimana and a shop run by Cipac as sources. The cracker text jokes that saurians themselves seem to like them.

7.content:
Daily Life in Natlan (also: Natlanese daily life, everyday life in Natlan, Natlanese customs): Everyday life in Natlan, the Pyro nation of war, is hot, loud and physical. People belong to one of six tribes, and each tribe is bonded with its own kind of Saurian, the evolved dragons that live alongside humans. Conflict is treated as an honest way to settle matters, many adults can fight, and music, dancing and showing off are everyday pleasures. Hot springs draw tourists, miners work phlogiston-rich ore, and loose clothing is the answer to the climate.

The six tribes are the Children of Echoes (Nanatzcayan), Scions of the Canopy (Huitztlan), People of the Springs (Meztli), Flower-Feather Clan (Tlalocan), Masters of the Night-Wind (Mictlan) and Collective of Plenty (Teteocan). Each is run by its own Chief, and no single Natlanese populace answers to one ruler; the Pyro Archon handles national matters rather than tribal affairs. Natlan has no formal army: each tribe fields its own warriors.

Outsiders' remarks give the flavour. The Inazuman Aikawa Susumu, who soaked in its hot springs, called Natlan a country of red-hot passion in name and climate. The Fontainian sailor Lectoure would choose it as the first place to settle down, while worrying about its many tribes and rules. A man named Adel at Bayda Harbor praises its people as energetic and forged for battle from birth, and stresses that they are not barbarians.

For roughly five hundred years the daily threat of the Abyss shaped ordinary life, and many able-bodied Natlanese are at least familiar with combat. Until the Night Kingdom was cleansed, people generally did not leave the nation at all, because their tribe's Wayob protected them from constant Abyssal influence. Since then travel abroad has been possible. That change is recent, so scenes set now can show a society getting used to open borders.

Practice: Common routines: tribal work (mining, delivering, guiding, patrolling, shamanic watching, farming), training with weapons, caring for a Saurian companion, music and dance, soaking in hot springs, and settling disputes by contest.

Each tribe has its own economic niche. The Children of Echoes mine, smith and appraise gems, and are Natlan's only source of obsidian, used in rituals such as communing with the Night Kingdom. The People of the Springs live largely from tourism, especially their famous hot springs. The Scions of the Canopy take delivery and hunting commissions and host visitors for extreme sports such as rock climbing, rappelling, bungee jumping and volcano parkour. The Collective of Plenty farm fertile land, trading or giving away surplus to other tribes; Varesa's family farm sells produce abroad, for example to the Fontainian chefs Escoffier and Dori. The Flower-Feather Clan are rangers and riders, and the Masters of the Night-Wind are priests and shamans who watch the ley lines and phlogiston.

Saurians are partners, not pets. They can choose their human companion and refuse anyone they do not accept. They understand human speech but humans cannot understand theirs; long association lets tribe members read a Saurian's body language and mood. Saurians have territories whose borders other Saurians respect, and these borders largely mark the Natlanese tribal lands as well.

Conflict is called "reason" in Natlan: parties are expected to face their own desires honestly, then decide the outcome by contest. When a dispute cannot be resolved, "peacemakers" such as Chasca may step in.

Technology builds partly on the ancient dragon civilisation. Phlogiston, a natural high-temperature energy, powers many tools, and Phlogiston Engravings imitate the Iridescent Inscriptions the dragons used; they can store information and create Spiritways. Much dragon technology (called the "Secret Source") is lost or undeciphered, and survives mainly in automatons. Many phlogiston vehicles come from the Children of Echoes: Kachina's drill, Chasca's flying cannon, Mavuika's all-terrain motorcycle and Xilonen's portable DJ set; the wiki credits Xilonen with building all of these. Jetpacks called Phlogiston Wings were designed by Tepal and finished by his mother Allpa after he died in the effort; they are rarely distributed, so most people use more traditional transport.

Tribal crafts: the Children of Echoes use drills at many scales and keep an enormous one above their settlement; the People of the Springs press circular record discs (also playable on Fontainian record players), make string and percussion instruments, and build artificial hot springs deliberately cooler than natural ones; the Masters of the Night-Wind weave scrolls recording events, with weavers for major events appointed by the Iktomisaur Elder Tlapo; the Flower-Feather Clan use hot air balloons to hold wooden platforms aloft.

Tribal warriors favour swords, clubs, spears, javelins, giant hammers, saw-like weapons and hand cannons, plus oversized gear such as collapsible slingshots, circular saws and portable cannons. Many dress or fight in imitation of their tribe's Saurian, and can use some of its elemental or special abilities, such as levitation, telekinesis or "surfing" on land, to a degree that depends on skill.

An Inazuman character, Shousen, remembered Natlanese boxers practising by imagining an opponent's moves, a method that inspired Shousen to develop Shinryuu, the Inazuman martial art featured in the limited-time Phantom Flow event. Saurians are poached by criminal groups in the modern day, and during Och-Kan's era humans subjugated them.

Regional variation: Tribal homes differ. The Children of Echoes live in Tequemecan Valley in the east; the Scions of the Canopy on Coatepec Mountain in the southeast; the People of the Springs at Toyac Springs in the south; the Flower-Feather Clan on Quahuacan Cliff; the Masters of the Night-Wind in the Tezcatepetonco Range; and the Collective of Plenty at Atocpan. Their Chiefs are Pacal, Wayna, Amina, Mutota, Biram and Acatl respectively. Each tribe pairs with a Saurian: Tepetlisaurus, Yumkasaurus, Koholasaurus, Qucusaurus, Iktomisaurus and Tatankasaurus.

Chiefs oversee their tribe's customs and can change them, and even the Pyro Archon cannot overrule them provided their tribe agrees. There is no age requirement: being chosen by the previous Chief and able to bear the duties is enough. Amina, Chief of the People of the Springs, is a young girl chosen by her grandfather and confirmed by the elders. The present Chiefs are on good terms but busy.

The Easybreeze Holiday Resort (also Tenochtzitoc, said to mean "cavern of stone and prickly pears") is a sparsely inhabited island off Natlan's westernmost edge, added in 5.8 as the first permanent summer-themed map. The wiki describes it as where the war began and met its end. The Tenochtzitoc were an Anemo tribe exiled in the past, while other exiled Muratans went on to settle in Mondstadt. The resort has a market and a leisure atmosphere distinct from the tribal homelands.

Saurian traits differ: young Yumkasaurs like having their ears touched but dislike tail grooming, and adults are proud to show off groomed tails; Qucusaurs are proud and, particularly with the Flower-Feather Clan, will carry a rider only if they sense no hesitation, since a rider's mistake could badly hurt both; Iktomisaurs can live over two centuries and meditate often; Tatankasaurs are docile until angered, then unreasonable until spent.

Scene use: Good hooks: a hot-spring visit where an outsider must first acclimate in a cooler artificial pool; a tribal contest or dance-off; a Saurian that refuses a new companion; a miner showing obsidian; a courier from the Scions; a friendly argument settled as a bout. Tone is warm, boisterous and competitive, with open pride in tribe.

Time sensitivity matters. Before the Night Kingdom was cleansed, the Natlanese seldom left and the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame (the tournaments tied to the Night Warden Wars) was an ever-present, costly institution. After it, the Pilgrimage was revised into athletic competitions, the old Bloomflower Trials returned, and the Natlanese could travel. Do not place Natlanese characters abroad in earlier-era scenes without a reason.

8.comment: Daily Life in Natlan: Natlanese Tribes in Daily Life
8.content: The six tribes use Nahuatl-style names: Nanatzcayan (Children of Echoes, Geo, miners), Huitztlan (Scions of the Canopy, Dendro, couriers and explorers), Meztli (People of the Springs, Hydro, guides), Tlalocan (Flower-Feather Clan, Pyro, rangers and riders), Mictlan (Masters of the Night-Wind, Cryo, shamans) and Teteocan (Collective of Plenty, Electro, farmers and wrestlers). Each tribe's Wayob grants Ancient Names to worthy members, who are revered and have their deeds recorded.

9.comment: Daily Life in Natlan: Saurian Companions
9.content: Saurians are the evolved descendants of Natlan's Pyro vishaps, who lost their ancient wisdom after the Heavenly Principles' conquest (Kukulkan and Och-Kan saw this as devolution). They cannot speak human language, except Cacucu, who copies a few phrases of Ifa's; Ajaw, a surviving older dragon, can communicate with both humans and Saurians. Saurians choose their companions and follow emotion and trust. Large wild flocks of Qucusaurs live in Ochkanatlan and the Great Volcano of Tollan. Little One, a Saurian with a red mark called the Flamelord's Blessing, shows that marked Saurians have stronger powers.

10.comment: Daily Life in Natlan: Phlogiston Tools and Vehicles
10.content: Phlogiston Engravings imitate dragon Iridescent Inscriptions to store information and create Spiritways. "Secret Source" refers to undeciphered draconic technology, mostly automatons (Dragon Cannons, Dragon Idols, combat constructs) that react to Nightsoul's Blessing. Phlogiston Wings jetpacks were designed by Tepal and finished by Allpa after his death; few exist. Xilonen built the other well-known phlogiston vehicles and her DJ set.

11.comment: Daily Life in Natlan: Easybreeze Holiday Resort Life
11.content: A sparsely inhabited island off Natlan's westernmost edge, also called Tenochtzitoc, the first summer-themed map permanently added to the game (5.8). Its subareas include the Concealed Land of Enigmas, Colorfall Cliffs, Easybreeze Market and Tete Isle. Prickly pears, which the name refers to, no longer grow there.

12.content:
Natlan Fashion (also: Natlanese fashion, Natlanese clothing, Natlan clothing, Natlan attire, Natlan dress): Dress in Natlan responds to a hot climate and a culture where fighting is part of daily life. Loose, light clothing is common (a visitor from Fontaine finds even her lightest dress too warm), and many adults wear markings on their bodies. Warriors in particular favour looks that echo their saurian companions, a habit also reflected in the Sauroform Tribal Warrior enemy groups. Each of the six tribes has its own NPC attire in the game, but canon gives few written details of what separates one tribe's dress from another's; the clearest tribe-level traits are the Children of Echoes' love of gemstone decoration and the masks of the Collective of Plenty wrestlers.

Because the wiki documents Natlanese fashion mostly through NPC model galleries, treat it as a visual vocabulary rather than a rulebook: bare midriffs, open chests, full coverage for children and the elderly, markings and tribe-specific details are patterns people have observed, not announced customs. Easybreeze Holiday Resort also has its own holiday-style NPC attire, distinct from the tribal mainland.

Practice: **Climate.** Natlan is hot, and clothing reflects it. The Fontainian traveller Baret says she was warned to dress light before setting out, and that among the People of the Springs even her lightest dress is not enough.

**Saurian imitation.** Natlanese people, especially warriors, like to wear things that make them look like their saurian companions. The Sauroform Tribal Warrior enemy groups show this: the Adventurer Handbook says warriors who live and fight beside saurians have gradually taken on their traits. The Search Chronicle event (Burning Up!) shows a hat inspired by this fashion, and the event character Ranjit is the source of the remark that warriors dress in imitation of their saurians.

**Masks.** Some members of the Collective of Plenty (Teteocan) wear masks as part of a long-standing wrestling tradition. According to the wiki, when two masked wrestlers duel, the loser removes the mask and the winner keeps theirs, so the winner stays a figure of mystery who inspires challengers. The tribe also wrestles its saurians, the Tatankasaurus, as an old tradition.

**Body markings and coverage.** Many adults wear markings on their bodies. Community observation of NPC models adds that children and the elderly are usually fully covered, that men may wear loose clothing leaving the chest and midriff bare or full coverage like other nations, and that women usually show the midriff. None of this is stated in game text.

**Gems.** The Children of Echoes treat stone as one of their symbols, and some describe gemstones as a second layer of skin. Members often decorate tools, weapons and accessories with gems, which some regard as a sign of skill or status.

**Ceremonial materials.** Obsidian is described as a very important ceremonial material in Natlan, and a character named Vichama says the Nanatzcayan (Children of Echoes) are its sole producers. This ties the tribe's stonework to ritual objects, though the sources read do not say it is worn as clothing.

**Easybreeze Holiday Resort.** The wiki lists separate NPC attire for the resort island, also called Tenochtzitoc, a sparsely inhabited island off the westernmost edge of Natlan. This is holiday-style dress, not a tribe's costume.

**Warrior types.** The Sauroform Tribal Warriors come from all six tribes, and each fights with its tribe's element. The saurian-crowned warriors are the clearest in-game view of the imitation fashion.

**NPC attire by tribe.** The wiki lists model galleries of boys', girls', men's, women's and, for several tribes, elderly attire for each of the six tribes plus the resort. The galleries show variety within each tribe (several men's and women's versions), but without text naming or explaining the garments, a roleplay description should stay at the level of tribal variation instead of inventing garment names.

**Character cards.** The Natlan Character Cards use a large circle with six tribal emblems around it. This is interface design, not clothing.

Regional variation: - **Children of Echoes (Nanatzcayan):** miners and gem appraisers who decorate tools, weapons and accessories with gems.
- **Collective of Plenty (Teteocan):** known for strength and agriculture; some wrestlers wear masks, and wrestling is a tribal tradition.
- **Scions of the Canopy (Huitztlan):** explorers, messengers and hunters living with Yumkasaurs; no dress detail in the text read.
- **People of the Springs (Meztli):** guides and cartographers; Baret finds the heat too much for her lightest dress there.
- **Flower-Feather Clan (Tlalocan):** Qucusaur riders and aerial warriors; no written dress detail beyond their riding role.
- **Masters of the Night-Wind (Mictlan):** shamans and people close to the Night Kingdom; no written dress detail.

The tribal emblems appear consistently on Natlan Character Cards, but the sources read give no list of tribal colours, patterns or garments. Do not assign colours to tribes unless canon is checked.

Scene use: - A traveller from another nation may be overheated and underprepared, as Baret is.
- A warrior might wear something that evokes their saurian companion's look.
- A Children of Echoes character might show off a gem-decorated tool or accessory as a point of pride.
- A Collective of Plenty wrestling match can involve masks: the loser unmasks, the winner stays masked.
- Avoid inventing named garments, tribal colours or meanings for body markings; canon does not give them.

13.content:
Religion in Natlan (also: Natlanese religion, Natlan faith, ancestor worship in Natlan, worship of the Wayob, Pyro Archon veneration): Natlan's faith is lived rather than preached. Each of the six tribes honours a Wayob, an ancestral spirit in the Night Kingdom where the dead go. A sacred fire, the Sacred Flame, burns in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. Warriors carry Ancient Names, and the Pyro Archon, a mortal who wins the throne in battle, tends the Flame.

Four things anchor belief. The Wayob give protection and, through the chief's dreams, guidance. The Night Kingdom is both the afterlife and, in practice, Natlan's ley lines. The Sacred Flame is a channel to that realm and is fuelled by the Contending Fire of warriors' battles. Ancient Names preserve the deeds of heroes. Natlan's gods are not remote: the Pyro Archon is a human champion, and the first one, Xbalanque, set the rules the nation still follows.

For five centuries the faith was also a wartime arrangement. The Wayob guarded the Night Kingdom against the Abyss, the Pilgrimage chose warriors for the Night Warden Wars, and the Ode of Resurrection let the Archon bring fallen Name bearers back. That war ended in the 5.x Archon Quest, so the practices below are described in both their wartime form and as they stand after it.

The belief system is layered. Some of it is old tribal ancestor worship, some was shaped by the dragon Kukulkan teaching the tribes about Phlogiston, and some rests on arrangements with higher powers (the Lord of the Night, and the Ruler of Death Ronova) that most Natlanese do not see. Canon gives no formal creed, scripture or priesthood hierarchy. Do not invent doctrine; present belief as customs, rites and stories.

Practice: Chiefs receive the will of their tribe's Wayob in dreams. People who die go to the Night Kingdom. Warriors draw Nightsoul power from it. The Pyro Archon enters the Sacred Flame to fetch fallen heroes in the Ode of Resurrection.

Wayob and tribe: each tribe has its own Wayob, called on for protection and blessings, and the tribe's chief is understood to hear its will in dreams. Villages keep an obsidian totem or black stone through which a Wayob can manifest as a Wayob Manifestation, though no one knows exactly why a Manifestation appears; it is believed to be sent to solve a problem. The Wayob choose which tribe members inherit Ancient Names.

The dead: when a Natlanese person dies they enter the Night Kingdom, where they gradually lose their sense of self and join the sea of souls. These souls are called Nightsouls, and warriors draw on them for Nightsoul's Blessing. The Night Kingdom accepted only Natlanese souls and kept only Natlanese memories; since Capitano's sacrifice (see below) it accepts people from other nations.

Ancient Names: an Ancient Name is an honorific linked to a quality such as Resilience (Uthabiti) or Unity (Umoja), with an obsidian feather-shaped stone on which glowing characters spell it. It carries the deeds of all earlier bearers, so passing it on keeps a tribe's history alive. Names normally grant no special power; the bearer earns their place. Six Names (Baraka, Malipo, Umoja, Vuka, Bidii, Uwezo) belong to the Heroes of Natlan.

The Sacred Flame: a flame that burns without stopping in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. It is a channel to the Night Kingdom and a way to speak with the Wayob. When a Pyro Archon ascends, it gives them the knowledge and memory of the land. It is fed by Contending Fire, produced only when Natlanese warriors fight each other, which is why the Pilgrimage exists.

The Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame: a tournament held at the Stadium. Before the war ended it picked the strongest warriors, fuelled the Flame, and doubled as the Natlanese way of testing a future Pyro Archon in battle. Outlanders could not take part because Contending Fire can only come from Natlanese fighters. Now it is a purely athletic competition; Kinich won the first of these.

Ode of Resurrection: a solemn rite at the Stadium. An officiant speaks a eulogy, the Archon steps into the Flame to find the fallen warrior and their Ancient Name in the Night Kingdom, the crowd bows and sings a song in Swahili, and the Archon walks out with the resurrected person. It worked only for Ancient Name bearers whose team had at least one member return victorious; a team that fell entirely was not revived, and its Names were forgotten, hence the saying that victors burn bright and losers turn to ash. It was discontinued when the Night Warden Wars ended.

Speaker's Chamber: beside the Stadium, presided over by the Pyro Archon. By tradition the tribal chiefs gather there by the flame at set intervals to negotiate. It also seems to act as Natlan's main judicial body, though that is only a suggestion on the wiki.

Obsidian: only the Children of Echoes produce it, and it is used for ritual objects, Ancient Name stones and communion with the Night Kingdom. The Masters of the Night-Wind are the tribe closest to the spirit realm and offer divination, blessing of tools and weapons, and similar services.

Turnfire Night: the Scions of the Canopy mark it each year, using a small flame split from the Sacred Flame. It remembers Yupanqui, who stole the Turnfire from the tyrant Och-Kan and fell into the Night Kingdom.

Name Engravers: a skilled smith can forge a new Ancient Name, usually on the Archon's commission. It costs part of their lifespan. Xilonen says the technique is simple but the research is not: the engraver must gather the subject's life story accurately, because falsehoods make a flawed Name that can cause cognitive problems for its bearer. Names can also be forged to record a dead person's life and later given by a Wayob to a worthy recipient; the wiki says it is unclear how often this is the origin of Names.

A tribe that fell from favour: the Muratans, an Anemo tribe, were exiled over a civil war more than 1,000 years ago; some settled in Mondstadt and the rest lived at Tenochtzitoc, where the Abyss struck at the Cataclysm. Tenoch lost his Ancient Name while still alive, which Mavuika says was likely due to his status as an exile.

The Traveler's Name, Tumaini (Hope): normally only Natlanese memories can form a Name. After the Traveler rescued Kachina and helped repel the Abyss, Mavuika promised them one. The Lord of the Night gave Citlali and Xilonen a Pilgrim's Chronicle to record the Traveler's deeds in place of the Night Kingdom, and later spoke the Name's incantation to unlock the Traveler's Nightsoul's Blessing.

Absence of rules: canon never lists commandments, holy days beyond those named, or a priestly class. When writing scenes, rely on the specific rites above.

Regional variation: All six tribes share the Night Kingdom, the Sacred Flame and Ancient Names but each has its own Wayob, its own Saurian companion and its own rites. The Masters of the Night-Wind are the most spiritual tribe.

Children of Echoes (Nanatzcayan): miners and obsidian-workers who forge Ancient Names; chief Pacal. Scions of the Canopy (Huitztlan): the Turnfire Night tribe, birthplace of Mavuika; chief Wayna. People of the Springs (Meztli): hot-spring keepers and guides; chief Amina. Flower-Feather Clan (Tlalocan): sky patrols and Qucusaur riders; chief Mutota. Masters of the Night-Wind (Mictlan): shamans who see souls and monitor ley lines and Phlogiston; chief Biram. Collective of Plenty (Teteocan): farmers and wrestlers, some of whom wear masks in a wrestling tradition; chief Acatl.

Saurians: the dragons of Natlan, descended from the ancient dragons after the Heavenly Principles' conquest, who lost their intelligence over time. Each tribe bonds with one kind of Saurian (Tepetlisaurs, Yumkasaurs, Koholasaurs, Qucusaurs, Iktomisaurs, Tatankasaurs), and Natlanese warriors often dress in imitation of their companions. Saurians choose their human partner and refuse anyone they do not acknowledge. They have their own language that humans learn to read only through long association. A rare red mark known as the Flamelord's Blessing is regarded as dangerous, and Saurians carrying it were traditionally sent back to the Night Kingdom unless the companion attempted a ritual at the Great Volcano of Tollan with the fallen dragon Xiuhcoatl; the wiki says that ritual was considered outdated because it almost never worked. Later quests reveal that Kukulkan deliberately controlled the expression of this mark.

Mictlan scrolls: the Masters of the Night-Wind weave scrolls that record important events in Natlan, appointed by the Iktomisaur Elder Tlapo.

Attitudes to dragons changed over time. In Och-Kan's era, Saurians were subjugated and one man was condemned to death for protecting his tribe's Saurians. The overthrow of Och-Kan returned authority to the tribes, restored their link to the Night Kingdom, and repaired relations with Saurians. Today there are still poachers, but the tribes live in harmony with their companions.

Outside views: Neuvillette likens war in Natlan to an undying flame. Foreign visitors such as Adel in Bayda Harbor describe the Natlanese as people whose souls are forged for battle from birth but who are not barbarians. These are outsider impressions, not doctrine.

Scene use: Show faith through objects and habits: obsidian stones, a village totem, the Flame glowing above the Stadium, names carried like heirlooms. Natlanese characters talk about the dead and their ancestors plainly, without hushed awe.

Natlanese characters speak of "the Night Kingdom" as a real place their ancestors went to, and of the Wayob as caring, sometimes overworked, ancestors. They use the Ancient Names of heroes as inspiration. Do not turn the Pyro Archon into a distant deity: Mavuika is a person who won the title, and the Natlanese treat Archons as champions, not untouchable gods. Visitors from other nations may find the openness about death and war surprising.

Before the war ended, leaving Natlan needed a chief's approval through the Wayob because their protection did not reach beyond the border; the wiki says the Wayob's absence could cause memory loss, stress and bad luck. This restriction has lapsed, and asking the chief is now a fading formality. Resurrection scenes are over: the Ode is retired, so a death in a present-day scene should not be reversed by the Archon unless canon supports it.

Respect the ambiguity about the gods behind the system. A character who knows about the Lord of the Night or Ronova should be someone who was present for it (the Traveler, Mavuika, Citlali, the Heroes of Natlan, and so on). An ordinary tribesperson knows the Wayob and the Flame, not the arrangements with the Shades.

14.content:
The Wayob are entities in the Night Kingdom that the six tribes venerate as the embodied will of their ancestors. They can see past and future and are described as will without form or thought. Each tribe calls on its own Wayob for protection and blessings, and its chief receives the Wayob's will in dreams. The Wayob choose who inherits an Ancient Name. They cannot extend their protection beyond Natlan without spending strength needed against the Abyss, so Natlanese who left risked memory loss, stress and bad luck. After the Abyss invaded the Night Kingdom, the Wayob were infected with Abyssal energy and their link to the people weakened. After the Night Kingdom was cleansed they resumed their duties, and told Citlali that Xbalanque was coming back.

Known Wayob include Chaac and Angakuk (tribes unnamed), a "Great Spirit of This Land" tied to the Children of Echoes, and and "Maghan's Master" (Masters of the Night-Wind). The Lord of the Night's page credits a human named Chaac with first contacting the Night Kingdom, leading to the creation of the Wayob; a Wayob also named Chaac is listed, and the pages read do not say whether they are the same. The wiki notes the word comes from the Mayan "way."

key: kingdom of the Lord of the Night
15.content:
A realm that the Wayob and the souls of the dead inhabit, described as a space between body and mind, life and death. It lies deep underground and works as Natlan's ley lines, since the original lines were wrecked in the War of Funerary Flame. The Lord of the Night built it from fragments of those lines on the advice of Ronova, and Xbalanque later strengthened it. Natlanese souls there are Nightsouls, which warriors draw on. Memories gathered there did not match those of the outside world, so the Night Kingdom could not record deeds done outside Natlan. At the Cataclysm the Abyss overran it, and the Wayob fought it for five centuries.

The Weaver of Secrets, a Dragonlord, merged her consciousness into the Night Kingdom to make a dream labyrinth where dead dragons and humans find peace, and keeps a pact of protection with the Masters of the Night-Wind. The Abyss was purged when the Traveler and Mavuika defeated Gosoythoth. Mavuika planned to give her life to restore the realm, but Capitano gave his life instead, merging his life force with the Lord of the Night and rewriting the lines' rules, so non-Natlanese are now accepted there.

16.content:
A fire that burns continually in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, called K'ahk' in the ancient tongue. It works as a conduit to the Night Kingdom and a way to communicate with the Wayob, and was the foundation of resistance against the Abyss. A new Pyro Archon receives the knowledge and memories of Natlan from it. It is fed by Contending Fire from battles between Natlanese warriors, and objects imbued with it can be burned to sustain it. It has several outlets: above the arena, in the Speaker's Chamber's fire pit, and in the Night Kingdom.

Five hundred years ago Mavuika placed her life in the Flame so that she could return when the tribes were ready. When the Pilgrimage was suspended and Contending Fire ran short, she sacrificed her own Archon power to keep it lit. Gosoythoth's manifestation briefly put it out, and Mavuika used the Pyro Gnosis to relight it. From the Flame in the Night Kingdom the two drew A Thousand Blazing Suns against Gosoythoth.

17.comment: Religion in Natlan: Pyro Archon succession
17.content:
Pyro Archons are born human and win the position through battle, and they age and die like other mortals; Natlan has had many. The first, Xbalanque (divine name Haborym, Ancient Name Kiongozi), defeated the Pyro Dragon Xiuhcoatl about 2,000 years ago and set up the rules that let ordinary people ascend. The Pilgrimage is how a new Archon is chosen. Mavuika, of the Scions of the Canopy, is the current Archon and was also the Archon at the Cataclysm. Named earlier Archons include a scarlet-eyed youth of the Flower-Feather Clan who succeeded Xbalanque, Cochanina, Gloharry, Shulevitz and Isaja.

Xbalanque borrowed power from Ronova, the Ruler of Death, to establish the Ode and Pilgrimage and made a bet with her: if humanity won against the Abyss, he could see the new Natlan for one day. Those who use her power are fated to die; Mavuika used it in the final battle and Ronova demanded her life, but Capitano's death was substituted. According to the Belyi Tsar, the Heavenly Principles had instead anointed Och-Kan as Sacred Lord and Xbalanque's succession defied Fate. In the present day Xbalanque returned for a day in Mausau's body, fought Mavuika in a spirit-level duel and lost narrowly, then left.

18.comment: Religion in Natlan: Lord of the Night
18.content:
Yohualtecuhtin is the ruler and god of the Night Kingdom, once an Angel of the same kind Seelies descended from. She made the Night Kingdom with Ronova's guidance and, in ancient times, guided the tribes. Abyssal corrosion left her weakened and asleep until Capitano woke her with the Secret Source mechanism. She agreed to sacrifice herself for Natlan, but Mavuika refused, and she gave Citlali and Xilonen the Pilgrim's Chronicle for the Traveler. When Capitano gave his life instead, she absorbed his life force and became essentially immortal. She named the Traveler's Ancient Name, Tumaini.

In ancient times the tribes reached her with obsidian and with live human sacrifices, often prisoners of war, and she told them to spread the Essence of Sacrifice on sterile ground to make it habitable for humans, a practice the wiki compares to Watatsumi's Goryou Matsuri. When Och-Kan banned worship of the Wayob and the Lord of the Night, a Nameless Priest believed her anger had cursed the people of Ochkanatlan with a horrific transformation. That was one man's belief, not confirmed.

19.comment: Religion in Natlan: Och-Kan and the banned faith
19.content:
Och-Kan, a half-dragon, half-human tyrant, took power after Xbalanque entered the Sacred Flame and proclaimed himself Sacred Lord. He banned live sacrifice and forbade people to worship the Night Kingdom, so as to consolidate power and keep humanity from being "strung up" by the Lord of the Night. The tribes gave their authority to a Grand Alliance and the dragons and Saurians were persecuted. After the Scarlet-Eyed Youth and his party overthrew him, sovereignty returned to the six tribes, who restored their link to the Night Kingdom and made peace with the Saurians.

Och-Kan's mind and body were later separated: the body became the Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash, and the mind the spirit Cocouik, who helps the Traveler in Ochkanatlan. Before dying, Och-Kan passed the Golden Entreaty to the Saurian Little One. His spirit returned to the Night Kingdom and helped the Traveler there. See his own entry for his history.

20.content: A fire from the Grand Alliance era used by Och-Kan to kill and oppress. Its victims feel burning from behind and are burned if they look back. Yupanqui stole it and used it on Och-Kan's army, then glanced back and was consumed, burning for a hundred days before falling through the ley lines to the Night Kingdom, where legend says it still burns. Malipo became an Ancient Name; its bearers include Burkina and Kinich. The Scions of the Canopy hold a Turnfire Night each year in memory of their ancestors.

21.comment: Religion in Natlan: Ode of Resurrection
21.content: A rite performed in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame to bring Ancient Name bearers back from the Night Kingdom after they died in the Night Warden Wars. It needed at least one member of the bearer's team to return victorious. Kachina's Ode failed because the Abyss was disrupting the Night Kingdom, which led Mavuika to suspend the Pilgrimage. During the final invasion, Mavuika called on the Lord of the Night's power to extend the Ode's protection to all Natlanese warriors, and Kachina later led an Ode for Mavuika and the Traveler that restored the Flame. After the Night Warden Wars ended the rite was discontinued.

22.comment: Religion in Natlan: Ronova's Fall and Natlan
22.content: Ronova, a Shade created by the Heavenly Principles, guided the Lord of the Night in building the Night Kingdom about 6,000 years ago and, 2,000 years ago, let Xbalanque borrow her power to set Natlan's rules; the Heavenly Principles considered this overreach. After Mavuika used her power against Gosoythoth, Ronova claimed Mavuika's life, but Capitano's death stood in for it. In the 7.1 Snezhnaya Archon Quest, Ronova was defeated after exceeding her authority and died. No text read says how that affects the rules she granted Natlan.

23.comment: Religion in Natlan: Tribal Wayob manifestations and Saurian companions
23.content: Each tribe pairs one Saurian kind with one Wayob manifestation type: Tepetlisaurs and the Rock-Cavernous Wayob (Children of Echoes), Yumkasaurs and the Foliar-Swift Wayob (Scions of the Canopy), Koholasaurs and the Flow-Inverted Wayob (People of the Springs), Qucusaurs and the Burning-Aflame Wayob (Flower-Feather Clan), Iktomisaurs and the Biting-Cold Wayob (Masters of the Night-Wind), Tatankasaurs and the Thundering Wayob (Collective of Plenty). Saurian companions are chosen by the Saurian, not assigned.

24.content:
Tribal Society of Natlan (also: Natlanese tribes, tribes of Natlan, six tribes of Natlan, Natlan tribal society): Natlan has no single populace: everyone belongs to one of six tribes, each with its own chief, saurian species, territory and ancestral Wayob. They are the Children of Echoes, Scions of the Canopy, People of the Springs, Flower-Feather Clan, Masters of the Night-Wind and Collective of Plenty. The Pyro Archon handles national war, ritual and defence.

Chiefs set and change their tribe's customs, and even the Pyro Archon cannot overrule them while their tribe agrees. Each tribe has a trade niche, its own tribal warriors who imitate their saurian, and Ancient Name bearers chosen by the Wayob. Conflict is treated in Natlan as a way of reaching "reason": a decisive, sincere settling of scores.

The structure is old (the wiki dates the six tribes to Och-Kan's era, roughly 2,000 years ago) and was shaped by 500 years of constant Abyss war, which is why leaving the nation, the Pilgrimage and the Ancient Names work the way they do. After the war ended (5.x) the system stayed, but the pressures behind it eased.

Practice: **Chiefs.** A chief runs the tribe on its own terms, overseeing customs and able to change them. There is no age requirement: being picked by the previous chief and coping with the duties is enough. Pacal (Children of Echoes) found other ways to support his tribe through the post; Amina (People of the Springs) is a young girl chosen by her grandfather and voted in by the elders, and she handles many tasks without trouble. The current chiefs are on good terms, though their duties leave little time together.

**The Archon's role.** The Pyro Archon does not manage tribal internal affairs. They are responsible for national events (the Pilgrimage, the Night Warden Wars) and defence. In the past the tribes have been bitterly divided, especially when a new Archon was appointed, to the point that the Archon could not intervene.

**Wayob and Ancient Names.** Each tribe's Wayob grants an Ancient Name to a tribe member it judges worthy. Bearers are revered; their deeds are recorded with the name, and a bearer who fully embodies the Wayob's aspirations can tap the knowledge of earlier bearers. Only name bearers can fight in the Night Warden Wars, because the Pyro Archon's Ode of Resurrection does not work for others.

**The Pilgrimage.** The tribes hold tournaments to fuel the Sacred Flame (see the dedicated Pilgrimage entry): a team round, then individual duels whose winners form the team sent to the Night Warden Wars. Winners are honoured, and non-bearers who took part in the tournaments share the esteem.

**Leaving Natlan.** During the 500-year war Natlanese generally did not leave, because the Wayob shielded them from constant Abyssal influence at home. Someone who wished to leave asked their chief to seek the Wayob's permission, and success was slim. Outside the borders the protection weakened and long exposure to Abyssal energy followed; Bennett, taken out of Natlan, is the notable case of unexplained bad luck. Once the Night Kingdom was purified, people could leave without harm and the Night Kingdom began accepting people from other nations. The wiki says a chief's permission is still needed; see uncertainties.

**Warriors.** Natlan has no formal military. Each tribe fields its own warriors, who often copy their saurian's look and fighting style, use its element and abilities to a degree set by skill, and are skilled in unarmed combat and in weapons such as swords, clubs, spears, javelins, hammers, saw-like weapons and hand cannons. Because of the war, many able-bodied Natlanese have at least some familiarity with fighting.
**Language and saurians.** Saurians understand human speech but humans cannot understand them, although some, like Chasca, read their body language. Few can communicate in both directions; Ajaw is one who can.

**Defunct tribe.** The wiki lists an exiled Anemo tribe: some became the Muratans who left for Mondstadt, the rest were banished to Tenochtzitoc (where the Easybreeze Holiday Resort now stands) and died in the Cataclysm.

**Older festival.** The Bloomflower Trials also fed the Sacred Flame and could help heal sick saurians, but ended after a past attempt brought bloodshed and division, and because the Pilgrimage yielded more Contending Flame. They resumed after the Abyss war ended.

**Pilgrimage suspension.** After Kachina failed to return from a Night Warden War even though her team won, Mavuika suspended future pilgrimages because she could not find Kachina's Ancient Name. The wiki also says this prevented further casualties and division, as she knew the Contending Fire produced was not enough to sustain the Sacred Flame. After the Abyss was purged, Mavuika recast the Pilgrimage as athletic competitions.

**Fate of the dead.** The deceased usually go to the Night Kingdom, but a few exceptions risk being forgotten for good. A team that loses a Night Warden War cannot be revived by the Ode; their souls linger in the Night Kingdom and slowly fade.

Regional variation: | Tribe | Chief | Saurian | Element | Ancient Name |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Children of Echoes (Nanatzcayan) | Pacal | Tepetlisaurus | Geo | Baraka (Ixquieh, Sundjatta, Xilonen) |
| Scions of the Canopy (Huitztlan) | Wayna | Yumkasaurus | Dendro | Malipo (Yupanqui, Burkina, Kinich) |
| People of the Springs (Meztli) | Amina | Koholasaurus | Hydro | Umoja (Uenuku, Tupac, Mualani) |
| Flower-Feather Clan (Tlalocan) | Mutota | Qucusaurus | Pyro | Vuka (Lianca, Menilek, Chasca) |
| Masters of the Night-Wind (Mictlan) | Biram | Iktomisaurus | Cryo | Bidii (Sanhaj, Ororon) |
| Collective of Plenty (Teteocan) | Acatl | Tatankasaurus | Electro | Uwezo (Ahpub, Wanjiru, Iansan) |

Economic niches: the Nanatzcayan mine, smith and appraise gems, are Natlan's only source of obsidian (used for ritual, such as communing with the Night Kingdom) and engrave Ancient Names. The Meztli live on tourism, notably their hot springs, which Inazuma admired enough to imitate with Snezhnayan boilers. The Huitztlan take delivery and hunting commissions and host extreme sports. The Mictlan offer fortune-telling, blessings of tools and weapons, artisanal goods and the weaving of historical scrolls. The Teteocan grow high-quality produce, often giving or trading surplus, and some sell abroad (Varesa's family farm). The Tlalocan are elite warriors.

Craft and technology by tribe: the Nanatzcayan build many of Natlan's phlogiston-powered vehicles and drills; Xilonen made nearly everything of the kind apart from the Phlogiston Wings, which Tepal designed and his mother Allpa finished after Tepal died in the process. The Meztli make record discs compatible with Fontainian players, and artificial springs cooler than the natural ones. The Mictlan scroll weavers are appointed by the Iktomisaurus Elder Tlapo. The Tlalocan use hot air balloons to hold platforms aloft. Teteocan wrestling has a masked tradition: the loser of a duel between mask wearers must unmask while the winner stays masked.

Scene use: - A visitor is introduced through a tribe, never to "Natlan" in general; a chief's word binds that tribe only.
- Name bearers get respect and the recorded deeds of their predecessors; other tribe members are not belittled for lacking a name.
- Before the war ended (pre-5.x endgame), characters would rarely have met anyone from outside Natlan; afterwards free travel and a visiting Natlanese are plausible.
- Do not give the Archon authority over a tribe's private customs.

Colour: an NPC at Bayda Harbor describes Natlanese as energetic people with souls forged for battle who are not barbarians, fond of street graffiti, showing off fashionable trinkets, dancing and music. This is one character's view, not a rule. The Natlanese practice of shadow boxing, seen by the Inazuman traveller Shousen in his youth, inspired Inazuma's Shinryuu.

Examples: Pacal and Amina show that chiefs can be young or reshape their role; Bennett shows what leaving cost; Kachina's case led to the Pilgrimage's suspension.

Examples tied to people: Xilonen (Name Engraver of the Children of Echoes), Kinich (current Malipo bearer, Scions of the Canopy), Mualani (Umoja, People of the Springs), Chasca (Vuka, peacemaker), Ororon (Bidii), Iansan (Uwezo), Varesa (Collective of Plenty family farm).

25.comment: Tribal Society of Natlan: Natlan Tribal Chiefs
25.content: Pacal leads the Children of Echoes, Wayna the Scions of the Canopy, Amina the People of the Springs (a young girl chosen by her grandfather and voted in by the elders), Mutota the Flower-Feather Clan, Biram the Masters of the Night-Wind and Acatl the Collective of Plenty. A chief oversees and may change tribal customs; the Pyro Archon cannot overrule them while the tribe agrees.

26.comment: Tribal Society of Natlan: Natlan Leaving Custom
26.content: During the 500-year Abyss war, Natlanese seldom left, because the Wayob protected them from Abyssal influence at home; leaving required the chief to seek the Wayob's permission, rarely granted. Outside, protection weakened. After the Night Kingdom was purified, travel became safe. See uncertainties on whether a chief's permission is still required.

27.comment: Tribal Society of Natlan: Muratans and Tenochtzitoc
27.content:
An Anemo tribe exiled at some past time. One part left Natlan and later settled in Mondstadt as the Muratans (their fate is unknown); the rest were banished to Tenochtzitoc, away from the other tribes, and all died in the Cataclysm. The Easybreeze Holiday Resort now stands there.

This is a wiki summary; details of the exile are not established in the sources checked.

28.comment: Tribal Society of Natlan: Bloomflower Trials
28.content: An old Natlanese festival that fed the Sacred Flame and could help heal sick saurians. It fell out of use after a past attempt ended in bloodshed and division, and because the Pilgrimage gave more Contending Flame. It resumed after the Abyss war ended; the wiki says it helped Milray recover from an illness and Antu get past his regrets.

key: Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame
29.comment: Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame
29.content:
Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame (also: the Pilgrimage, Pilgrimage of the Sacred Flame): The Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame ("the Pilgrimage") is Natlan's great combat tournament at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. Fights between Natlanese produce Contending Fire, which fuels the Sacred Flame against the Abyss. Until the Night Warden Wars ended (5.3), the top-ranked Ancient Name bearers were sent to fight the Abyss in the Night Kingdom. Since then Mavuika has run it as a purely athletic competition.

Placing high brings instant fame, and in wartime winning was the highest honour in Natlan. Natlanese also say the Pilgrimage is how the Pyro Archon is chosen: anyone can take the title by proving themselves the mightiest warrior of their era.

Practice: In its wartime form there were two stages. Teams, usually captained by an Ancient Name bearer, fought each other for Contending Fire. The winning teams' members then fought one-on-one matches, and the top scorers won.

Contestants register at the Stadium, and on the eve the Weary Inn feeds and lodges them free at the Archon's expense. After the Archon's opening speech, teams are dropped by hot-air balloon at random spots. They win Fire at Fire Towers and must carry enough back before time runs out. Losing a fight, leaving the grounds or running out of time all mean elimination. In the individual stage, results decide each contestant's next opponent, so closely ranked rivals end up meeting.

- Registration: the pre-registration form has an optional page of hobbies and personal details, meant for the promotional team. Captains must register teams before the evening of the day before. Every Ancient Name bearer is expected to take part, as a duty.
- The eve: the Weary Inn is packed with revellers, and Mavuika can often be found there playing cards or singing.
- Punctuality: a late or oversleeping contestant gets the whole team disqualified.
- Team stage: monsters are placed on the grounds on purpose. Teams hand in their Fire by lighting the Sacred Flame at the Stadium. Teams rarely include more than one Ancient Name bearer, and doing so can look cowardly. Because the captain usually decides the team stage, weak bearers struggle to find teammates. The team stage is meant to teach warriors to fight together.
- Individual stage: lots set the first pairings. Commentators call the action from the stands and from the balloons.
- Close: the victors are announced on stage and receive the Archon's charge to go and defeat the Abyss.
- Conduct: contestants may only use the weapons and items recorded at registration. Losers must accept the result. Staff warn anyone who harasses contestants still in the running, and repeat offenders can be barred. Organisers say a few sore losers turn up every year.
- The Stadium is closed for maintenance after a Pilgrimage, and unannounced sparring or rehearsals in the main arena are forbidden.

Purposes: The wartime Pilgrimage did three things: it made Contending Fire for the Sacred Flame, it chose warriors for the Night Warden Wars, and by tradition it is how a Pyro Archon proves their claim. Contending Fire comes only from battles between people of Natlan, so outlanders were banned. Only victors with Ancient Names went to war, because the Ode of Resurrection works only on Ancient Name bearers, and only if at least one member of the team returns victorious.

Natlanese hold that battle is the most complete test of a future Archon, and that a clear victory is hard to dispute. Kachina told the Traveler that the current Archon won overwhelmingly. Mavuika has said the Pilgrimage and the war "have nearly always been linked": without a chance to fight the Abyss, rankings lose prestige, fewer people enter, and less Fire is made.

History: The Pilgrimage is old. Mavuika's father won one and went to war against the Abyss when she was a small child, before she became Archon. The most famous bearer of Kachina's Ancient Name fought in twenty-seven Night Warden Wars and still achieved top rankings in the Pilgrimage when he was over sixty. According to the NPC Karpa, it was held whenever the Abyss threatened, and more often as incursions worsened in recent years.
- 5.0: the tournament the Traveler watched. Five victors went to war: Chasca, Iansan, Kaiulani, Kibangu and Kachina. Their side won, but Mavuika's Ode of Resurrection failed to bring Kachina back, and Mavuika suspended the Pilgrimage "until this matter is resolved". Kachina was later rescued from the Night Kingdom.
- 5.3: after Gosoythoth was defeated and the Night Warden Wars ended, Mavuika announced the Pilgrimage's return as a purely athletic competition, to help Natlan move past the war.

Mavuika's character story shows what the old rite cost. Her father's team won after three days and nights of fighting but lost three of seven warriors, her father among them. He was revived at the Rite of Rekindling. The Ode reverses only the fatal wound, though, not injuries built up over a long battle or illnesses he already had, and he came back too broken to stand.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Pilgrimage is a sports contest, no longer a prelude to war, and outsiders may now enter. Kinich was the first champion of the new format.

Mavuika says it remains a trial to find the strongest and a stage for each contestant to show their growth. No later Pilgrimage appears in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) content.

Regional variation: The custom is unique to Natlan, and all six tribes take part: the Children of Echoes, People of the Springs, Scions of the Canopy, Flower-Feather Clan, Collective of Plenty and Masters of the Night-Wind. Contestants are introduced by tribe, and each tribe helped prepare the 5.3 tournament. Chasca of the Flower-Feather Clan was announced as a victor "with her sixth consecutive win". Mualani had been to three Night Warden Wars, won each time, and never needed reviving.

Individuals relate to it differently. Years of losses brought Kachina ridicule from her playmates and doubts about whether she deserved her Ancient Name. Varesa is said to be knocked out quickly because she cannot bring herself to fight fellow Natlanese seriously. Kaiulani made a comeback after ten years without a win.

Scene use: Good scenes: the crowded Weary Inn on the eve; the Archon's speech under the Sacred Flame; balloon drops; tense waits for the match draw; friends drawn against each other in a final round. Check the era. Before the 5.0 suspension, victory meant war, and a team wiped out meant its members' Ancient Names were lost for good. From 5.3 on, it is a sports festival open to outlanders.

Between Kachina's failed Ode and the end of the war, the Pilgrimage was suspended, and the suspension frightened and divided people. Do not let an outlander compete in a wartime Pilgrimage, and do not treat the Ode as unlimited.

The Traveler and Paimon served as special supervisors at the 5.3 Pilgrimage, so the Traveler did not compete. A {{user}} from outside Natlan could plausibly enter a later athletic Pilgrimage, but that is an extrapolation; canon does not show one.

Examples: - Kachina's teammates left her on registration night for stronger captains. Kinich took over Mualani's team so that Mualani and Kachina could enter as a pair. In the final round, Kachina beat Mualani and took the last of the five victors' places.
- Tepexpan and Tamuin, both eliminated, tried to force a rematch on Kachina in the contestants' lounge and were warned off by staff. When her Ode failed, they led the doubts about her victory.
- At the 5.3 Pilgrimage, Kinich beat Nlteego in the final. Mavuika then picked out the reborn first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque, among the contestants: a boy the crowd took for Mausau, Tawto's grandson. By his own account he did not even reach the final 32.

- Citlali entered the 5.3 Pilgrimage, and Kinich locked his companion Ajaw in a chest so he could win on his own merit.

30.comment: Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame: Contending Fire
30.content: Contending Fire is the energy produced when people of Natlan fight one another, and it is the fuel of the Sacred Flame. During the Pilgrimage's team stage, contestants win it at Fire Towers and carry it back as Contending Sparks, small sparks "born from conflict" in the item text. They light the Sacred Flame with them. Objects carried in battle by Natlanese warriors also absorb some Contending Fire. In Past and Future, Mavuika burned such objects to release it. Fights involving outlanders reduce how much Fire is made, which is why outlanders were barred from the wartime Pilgrimage.

31.comment: Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame: Suspension of the Pilgrimage
31.content:
After the 5.0 Night Warden War, Mavuika's Ode of Resurrection could not find Kachina in the Night Kingdom. Sore losers in the crowd claimed she had not really won. Mavuika declared the victory and Kachina's part in it beyond doubt, apologised for the failed ceremony, and suspended the Pilgrimage to prevent more deaths. She rejected Chasca's idea of holding it without the war, because without the war the event would lose prestige and produce less Fire.

In private with Kinich and Iansan, Mavuika admitted the real reason. The Abyss's corrosion had already caused a massive Pyro shortage, and the Pilgrimage could not produce enough Contending Fire to make up for it. She hid this from the public to avoid panic and kept the Sacred Flame burning with her own power until the heroes were ready.

32.comment: Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame: The new Pilgrimage
32.content:
After the war ended, Mavuika remade the Pilgrimage as a pure athletic competition promoting fair play and personal growth: "competition in place of ceaseless battle." The tribes shared the preparations: supplies, cleaning and remodelling the venues, recruiting staff and even forecasting the weather. Iansan designed the events. The Traveler and Paimon were invited as special supervisors, which kept them out of the competition, and they followed the contestants around the course to check that it was run fairly.

The knockout round was a pursuit course: contestants chased a winged, fiery ball across varied terrain. It had a vertical section that Mavuika worried might make people dizzy. Other events included a ball-launcher challenge, since ball games are an old Natlanese tradition. The eight contestants with the highest total scores went on to final one-on-one battles, and only one champion was named. Kinich won by beating Nlteego in the final.
